Who We are? Target Engineering brings 50+ years of experience in EPC and industrial infrastructure. With in-house fabrication, marine expertise, and multidisciplinary capability, we deliver projects with scale, confidence, and care. Why Join Us? At Target Engineering, you’ll work on large-scale energy, marine, and civil infrastructure projects. Join a business with deep technical roots, where your voice is heard, your impact is visible, and your career is part of a legacy of excellence. Your Role As a Piping Quantity Surveyor , you will be responsible for the following key responsibilities, including but not limited to: Project Design & Planning Develop and review civil engineering designs, calculations, and technical deliverables for EPC projects. Prepare project schedules, identify key milestones, and monitor engineering deliverables. Ensure compliance with applicable local regulations, international codes, industry standards, and company procedures. Support bid preparation, technical evaluations, tender reviews, and proposal development. Site Supervision & Construction Management Oversee construction and site execution activities to ensure compliance with approved designs and project specifications. Monitor project progress, quality, safety performance, and productivity. Conduct routine site inspections, audits, and assessments. Identify and resolve engineering, construction, and interface-related issues. Prepare regular project progress reports and technical documentation. Multidisciplinary Coordination Coordinate closely with engineering, procurement, construction, commissioning, and operations teams. Interface with marine, power, oil & gas, and industrial plant disciplines to ensure seamless project integration. Work with procurement teams to evaluate and select suitable materials and equipment. Liaise with clients, consultants, contractors, vendors, and regulatory authorities. Risk Management & Compliance Perform risk assessments and implement mitigation plans throughout the project lifecycle. Ensure compliance with HSE policies, industry standards, and regulatory requirements. Promote a strong safety culture and support incident prevention initiatives. Quality Assurance & Control Implement quality control procedures for civil works and construction activities. Review contractor and subcontractor deliverables to ensure compliance with project requirements. Participate in inspections, audits, and final acceptance processes. Project Controls & Documentation Maintain accurate records of engineering deliverables, design changes, approvals, and technical submissions. Support budgeting, cost estimation, resource planning, and change management activities. Prepare material approval documentation, engineering reports, and project close-out records. Stakeholder Management Serve as a technical focal point for clients and project stakeholders. Build strong relationships with internal and external project teams. Ensure timely resolution of technical queries and stakeholder concerns. Continuous Improvement Identify opportunities to improve engineering practices, tools, and workflows. Stay updated with emerging technologies, industry best practices, and regulatory developments. What We’re Looking For Experience Minimum 6 years of experience in civil engineering, preferably within Oil & Gas EPC, energy, industrial, infrastructure, or large-scale construction projects. Master's Degree is an advantage. Professional Engineer (PE), Chartered Engineer (CEng), or equivalent industry-recognized certification preferred. Strong knowledge of civil engineering design principles, construction methodologies, and materials. Familiarity with project planning and scheduling tools such as Primavera P6 and MS Project. Experience conducting site surveys, inspections, and technical assessments. Sound understanding of quality, safety, and regulatory compliance requirements. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Expertise in risk identification and mitigation. Excellent communication and stakeholder management abilities. Ability to explain technical concepts to multidisciplinary teams. Strong organizational and project coordination skills. What We Offer The chance to contribute to some of UAE’s Oil and Gas EPC Mega projects. A collaborative, supportive environment that values innovation and excellence. Opportunities for professional growth and career progression. Competitive salary and benefits package. Ready to be part of our team? If you’re inspired by what you’ve read and believe you’re the right fit, we’d love to hear from you. Join Target Engineering and Construction Co. LLC and play a pivotal role in shaping a high-performing team that drives our success. Apply today and be part of something excellent!

review_candidates.title: Chief Program Officer
review_candidates.description: About Living Goods Community health is one of the most proven ways to save lives and we are seeing growing commitments and investments from African Governments towards Community Health Systems. But as systems scale, many governments struggle to maintain quality, control costs, and deliver consistent results. Scale without performance puts lives at risk. Living Goods is a government performance partner that helps countries build affordable, intelligent, high-impact community health systems. We work alongside governments to design, embed, and strengthen the operating foundations that make care delivery reliable, measurable, and continuously improving. At the center of our approach is our Performance Operating System for community health. And it’s aimed at scale from the start. We treat cost as a design parameter, helping governments maximize health impact within real budgets. We combine rigorous evidence with operational learning to understand what drives outcomes and improves performance. And we build intelligent systems that learn, adapt, and improve as they scale—using data, digital tools, and AI to strengthen performance over time. Founded in Uganda in 2007, Living Goods works alongside governments across Burkina Faso, Kenya, and Uganda to strengthen national community health systems. Our approach is backed by randomized controlled trials and has contributed to reductions in child mortality of more than 27%, while delivering life-saving care for about $2 per person served. About The Role Living Goods is hiring a Chief Program Officer to lead programs that bring life-saving health services to millions of families. The Chief Program Officer (CPO) provides strategic leadership and operational oversight across Living Goods' global program portfolio, ensuring high-quality, evidence-driven delivery at scale. The CPO sets program strategy and priorities, stewards the frameworks and tools that enable consistent country-level execution, and leads the organization's Performance, Evidence and Insights function, ensuring that robust evidence, learning, and performance insights drive strategic decision-making, program improvement, and organizational impact. The role also shapes Living Goods' innovation agenda, stewarding the pipeline of new approaches, tools, and delivery models from concept through adoption and scale to define the next frontier of community health impact. Critically, the CPO serves as the connective tissue between program and technology, ensuring that digital health tools and data systems are purposefully embedded into delivery models to strengthen community health worker performance and improve health outcomes. The CPO leads disciplined geographic expansion, strengthens donor and fundraising alignment, and ensures that program knowledge is systematically generated, captured, and shared across the organization, maximizing Living Goods' impact, efficiency, and scale Reporting Scope The Chief Program Officer (CPO) reports to the Chief Executive Officer and serves as a member of the Global Executive Team. The role provides strategic leadership and oversight across the organization's Performance, Evidence and Insights, Innovation, Program Strategy, and Country Incubation functions, with accountability for program strategy, budget stewardship, fund transfers, and decision-making as set out in Living Goods' Delegation of Authority Framework. Key Responsibilities Program Strategy & Portfolio Support: ( 30% of time) Provide strategic direction and shared capabilities that countries can draw on to strengthen impact, efficiency, and scale. Set global program strategy and priorities across existing and new initiatives, aligned with Living Goods' strategy and Theory of Change. Enable strategic portfolio prioritization and trade-offs, offering frameworks and insights to inform leadership decision-making. Shape geographic expansion and portfolio evolution, including criteria for scale, focus, consolidation, or exit. Set strategic direction for the innovation pipeline and its pathways to country adoption and scale. Build and steward strategic partnerships, including new government partnerships that countries can leverage where they add value. Shape fundraising priorities and decisions based on program strategy and performance insights. Execution for Impact: (20% of time) Strengthen country-level delivery performance by providing shared frameworks, digital and data tools, and performance oversight — ensuring technology serves as a force multiplier for program quality and efficacy. Design and steward global program frameworks, standards, and models based on evidence to guide consistent, high-quality delivery at country level. Own and evolve the performance operating system — including tools, practices, and ROI focus — used across countries. Enable cross-country performance review, learning, and continuous improvement. Drive and monitor the innovation stage gates to optimize innovation pipeline delivery and lifecycle. Serve as the programmatic voice in shaping how digital health tools are designed and deployed — partnering closely with the CTO to ensure technology investments are grounded in frontline delivery realities and community health worker needs, rather than owning the technology itself. Work with the technology team to ensure shared digital and data tools are fit-for-purpose, translating program requirements into actionable inputs for the technology roadmap. Ensure that digital tools genuinely support community health worker performance and that adoption is embedded in program quality standards. Improve ways of working, systems, and processes between global and country teams to reduce friction and duplication.. Performance, Evidence and Insights: (20 % of time) Generate decision-grade evidence and insights to inform strategy, strengthen programs, and improve outcomes. Ensure robust analytics, monitoring, and independent research and evaluations across programs and innovations to build credible evidence and learning. Generate and synthesize insights from data and evidence to inform program design, performance, and decision-making. Translate evidence into clear insights and narratives for countries, leadership, partners, and donors. Ensure the documentation and knowledge management system is effective in supporting learning, replication, scale, and the organization's thought leadership agenda. New Countries: (15% of time) Enable disciplined, repeatable expansion through a clear country scoping and incubation model. Define and apply criteria for scoping new countries, aligned to strategy and organizational capacity. Design and steward the new country incubation model, including time-bound global support. Support and oversee countries during incubation, including direct accountability for readiness and transition to a core country. Fundraising and Donor Delivery: (15% of time) Ensure programmatic integrity and alignment from proposal through delivery and reporting. Ensure funding proposals are programmatically sound. Provide programmatic input to donor engagement where technical credibility is required. Oversee delivery against grant commitments and surface risks early. Ensure accurate and coherent programmatic reporting. Leadership: (Across) Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing global programs team, fostering a culture of excellence, accountability, and continuous learning. Serve as a key member of the Senior Leadership Team, contributing to organizational strategy, culture, and cross-functional decision-making. Model Living Goods' values and champion equity, inclusion, and community-centred program design. Represent Living Goods externally with donors, partners, governments, and global health stakeholders. The Person We Are Looking For Living Goods is looking for a strategic program leader who has driven multi-country health delivery at scale and who works fluently across program and technology. This is a role defined by strategic leadership, evidence rigor, and the ability to translate program needs into technology priorities without owning technology delivery itself. What The Role Requires Master's degree or equivalent in public health, international development, business administration, or a related discipline preferred; bachelor's degree required. 15+ years of progressive leadership experience in global health, international development, or a related field, with significant time working in sub-Saharan Africa. Proven track record leading large-scale, multi-country program delivery — ideally in primary healthcare or last-mile service delivery. Demonstrated ability to work at the intersection of program and technology, translating digital health investments into measurable impact. Experience managing and developing senior teams across geographies and cultures. Track record of successful donor engagement, fundraising, and grant management. Private sector experience is a serious advantage. Bilingual French and English is a serious advantage. Willing to travel 30%+ of the time. Role based in Nairobi. How to Apply: Process Applications will be considered on a rolling basis until the position is closed. Early applications are strongly encouraged. Expressing Interest If you have questions about the role or wish to express interest, please write to Living Goods' recruitment team using the contact details below. Contacts Recruitment [email protected] Website: www.livinggoods.org

What You'll Do Brand Strategy & Positioning Own Factorial's global brand strategy, including positioning, architecture, identity, tone of voice, and corporate narrative. Lead the evolution of our brand as Factorial moves from an HR-focused platform to AI for Business, making our broader vision clear, credible, and compelling. Define what makes Factorial different in a market where many companies claim to be AI-powered, ensuring our brand is grounded in real product capabilities and customer value. Build a consistent global brand that resonates with different audiences, company sizes, and markets while allowing for meaningful local adaptation. Establish a clear framework for measuring brand impact, connecting awareness, consideration, branded demand, pipeline influence, and commercial performance. Creative, Content & Campaigns Lead our creative and content organisation, setting a high bar for quality, originality, and execution across every customer touchpoint. Develop distinctive campaigns and creative concepts that bring Factorial's vision to life and make complex ideas about AI and business operations easy to understand. Ensure consistency across brand campaigns, product launches, digital channels, events, sales materials, and customer communications. Build AI-enabled creative workflows that increase speed, experimentation, and localisation without compromising quality. Partner closely with Performance Marketing and Product Marketing to ensure brand creativity supports demand generation and business growth. Communications, PR & Media Own Factorial's global communications strategy, including corporate communications, media relations, executive communications, and issues management. Strengthen Factorial's presence in relevant business, technology, and industry media across our key markets. Shape our public narrative around AI for Business, helping customers, journalists, analysts, and the wider market understand our approach and its practical value. Lead communications around major company milestones, product launches, market expansion, and other strategic announcements. Work closely with People and leadership teams to ensure the experience inside Factorial reflects the values and ambition we communicate externally. Executive Visibility & Thought Leadership Position Factorial's founders and leadership team as credible, distinctive voices on AI, the future of work, and how businesses operate. Build a thought-leadership strategy that generates meaningful conversations through original perspectives, research, media opportunities, and industry events. Identify opportunities for Factorial to contribute to the conversations shaping the future of business software and AI. Act as a senior spokesperson for Factorial when appropriate, representing the company with clarity and conviction. Team & Organisational Leadership Lead and develop a multidisciplinary team across brand, creative, content, communications, and PR, working through senior leaders and building a strong leadership structure. Attract, develop, and retain exceptional talent across creative and communications disciplines. Establish clear priorities, objectives, and accountability, ensuring the team operates with focus, speed, and strong cross-functional collaboration. Build an environment where people take ownership, experiment, share knowledge, and continuously raise the quality of their work. Manage the Brand & Communications budget effectively, balancing long-term brand building with measurable business impact. What We're Looking For 15+ years of experience in brand, communications, or marketing, including significant leadership experience in a high-growth technology company. A proven track record of building and evolving brands in ways that influence business performance, not just awareness or creative recognition. Experience leading a major repositioning, category evolution, or transformation of a company's market narrative. Experience leading multidisciplinary teams across brand, creative, content, communications, and PR, with the ability to develop strong leaders. Excellent creative and editorial judgement, with the ability to set a clear direction while empowering teams to deliver. Strong commercial understanding and the ability to connect brand investment to business outcomes, including demand generation and pipeline contribution. Experience building meaningful relationships with media, industry stakeholders, and business leaders across relevant markets. Confidence communicating complex ideas clearly, both internally and externally, including with executive audiences and on stage. Strong cross-functional leadership skills, with experience partnering closely with Product, Sales, Marketing, and Finance. Fluency in English. Additional European languages are a plus. Nice to Have Experience in B2B SaaS, HR tech, fintech, business management software, or workflow automation. Experience positioning AI-powered products for business customers. Experience building a brand during a transition from a specialised product to a broader platform. Experience leading an in-house creative studio or bringing agency capabilities in-house. Experience using AI to improve creative production, content operations, and localisation at scale. Experience working across multiple European markets and balancing global consistency with local relevance. About Factorial Factorial is the AI for Business that knows companies, connects how work happens across the business, and turns that context into action. Founded in Barcelona in 2016, we now have +1,700 employees serving more than 16,000 companies across 112 countries. Factorial started with a simple idea: companies were spending too much time managing processes and not enough time doing the work they were hired to do: their best work. But as companies grow, work gets more disconnected. More people, more tools, more information, and more time spent connecting the dots. Generic AI can answer questions, but it doesn’t know your company. Every time, you have to give it the context. Factorial is different. Because it’s inside the company, it already knows how it works, including its people, processes, policies, and data. So you can ask it to do real work, from screening candidates and managing expenses to answering questions and creating reports. AI isn’t the goal. Giving people back their time is. When work changes, so do we. Our values We own it : We take responsibility for every project. We make decisions, not excuses. We learn and teach : We're dedicated to learning something new every day and, above all, share it. We partner : Every decision is a team decision. We trust each other. We grow fast : We act fast. We think that the worst mistake is not learning from them. Perks of Being Part of Our Team We care about people, and we also offer a lot of benefits for employees: High-growth, multicultural, and friendly environment Alan as private health insurance Healthy life with Wellhub (gyms, pools, outdoor classes) ♀ Save expenses with Cobee Language classes Breakfast in the office and organic fruit Nora discounts Free caffeine and theine ☕ Pet-friendly

review_candidates.title: Trade Show Coordinator
review_candidates.description: Trade Show Coordinator Oberursel, Germany | Full-time, permanent About Formulatrix Headquartered in Dubai, UAE, FORMULATRIX® is a rapidly growing, highly profitable company. Founded as a software company in 2002, we are now a global leader in laboratory automation hardware and software for the life sciences, including automated liquid handling, cell culture and protein crystallization systems, and filtration technologies. Our products are used by research scientists worldwide, including the top 50 pharmaceutical companies. Our business is international in scope, with offices across the United States, Europe, and Asia. Formulatrix Europe Limited supports our customers across Europe and the United Kingdom from our site in Oberursel, near Frankfurt. About the Role We are looking for a Trade Show Coordinator to join our growing European operation. Formulatrix runs more than 100 events worldwide each year, and this role sits at the centre of how we get our people, instruments, and materials to them on time safely. This is a hands-on position that combines coordination and research with practical logistics. You will help decide which shows we attend, own the freight and shipping paperwork that gets us there, and run the warehouse operation in Oberursel that supports it. You will work closely with our trade show team in Pakistan, our manufacturing site in Indonesia, and our global sales managers. The role offers real scope to grow. As our European events programme expands, so does the responsibility and the opportunity for the person in this seat. Depending on qualifications and experience, the gross annual salary for this position ranges from €55,000 to €70,000. What You Will Do Coordinate logistics with our trade show team in Pakistan, including shipping destinations, delivery windows, and receipt deadlines Prepare and manage all freight and courier documentation, obtain shipping quotes, and track shipments through to delivery and return Ship demonstration instruments to events and customer sites, and receive inbound inventory from our manufacturing site in Indonesia Run shipping and receiving at the Oberursel warehouse, including loading and unloading delivery trucks and operating a manual pallet jack Pack and prepare booth materials, displays, and demonstration equipment to a consistent standard so that everything arrives complete and on time Deliver supplies and equipment locally via van across Germany and neighbouring markets as required Maintain accurate event, shipment, and inventory records in our tracking spreadsheets and CRM Travel to two to three trade shows per year, typically up to one week each, to support booth build and dismantle What You Need Fluent German and strong business English, both spoken and written. You will work daily with colleagues in Pakistan and Indonesia and with German suppliers, organisers, and freight forwarders Demonstrated experience in logistics, freight forwarding, shipping and receiving, warehouse operations, or events operations. Valid Class B, C1, or C driving licence Precision with timing and deadlines. Events do not move, so materials have to arrive before they open Confident with spreadsheets, including basic analysis, filtering, and reporting Well organised and able to manage several shows in parallel at different stages Legally authorised to work in Germany Nice to Have Experience with international freight, customs documentation, or ATA carnets Prior exposure to trade shows, exhibitions, or conference logistics Experience working with a CRM or relational database. Full training on our system will be provided, so this is not required Experience coordinating across multiple time zones and international teams What We Offer A permanent, full-time position with a growing international company Structured onboarding and training from our European marketing lead Genuine growth path as our European events programme expands Exposure to the global life science research market and to customers advancing drug discovery and structural biology How to Apply To be considered for this position, please email jobs@formulatrix.com with the words " Trade Show Coordinator" in the subject line. The interview process is conducted in English, so please submit your CV in English (MS Word or PDF only) and answer the following questions in the body of your email: What are your salary expectations? When are you available to start? Are you authorised to work in Germany? Will you now or in the future require visa sponsorship to work in Germany? Do you hold a valid Class B driving license? Please describe your relevant logistics, shipping, or events experience. Only candidates who answer the questions above will be considered. No recruiters or agencies. Formulatrix is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of gender, age, origin, religion, disability, or sexual identity.

review_candidates.title: Trade Compliance Analyst
review_candidates.description: Who We Are; What We Do; Where We’re Going Magnet Forensics is a global leader in the development of digital investigative software that acquires, analyzes, and shares evidence from computers, smartphones, tablets, and IoT-related devices. We are continually innovating so our customers can deploy advanced and effective tools to protect their companies, communities, and countries. Serving thousands of customers globally, our solutions are playing a crucial role in modernizing digital investigations, helping investigators fight crime, protect assets, and guard national security. With employees based around the world, Magnet Forensics has been expanding our global presence. As a part of Magnet Forensics, you can expect to make a difference in the world, no matter what role you play. You’ll be supported through learning and development, not to mention an incredible team with unbelievable talent and integrity. If you think you would be the right person to join our team working towards this goal, we would love to hear from you! Role Summary Magnet Forensics is seeking a detail-oriented Trade Compliance Analyst to support the company's global trade compliance program. This is an entry-level to early-career position responsible for conducting daily compliance reviews and screening activities to ensure compliance with applicable export control, sanctions, and trade regulations, including the U.S. Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR). The successful candidate will perform Know Your Customer (KYC) reviews, restricted-party screening, sales opportunity reviews, end-user due diligence, and transaction monitoring activities. The position plays a critical role in helping the company identify potential export compliance risks before products, software, services, or technology are provided to customers, partners, vendors, or other third parties. This role will work closely with the Legal, Compliance, Sales Operations, Finance, Customer Success, and Procurement teams and will escalate higher-risk matters to senior compliance personnel for further review. The analyst will be responsible for screening transaction parties using Descartes and ensuring appropriate documentation and records are maintained. Magnet's procedures require screening customers, vendors, banks, brokers, consignees, and other transaction participants against restricted party lists throughout the transaction lifecycle. What You'll Do Customer and Transaction Due Diligence Conduct Know Your Customer (KYC) reviews of customers, resellers, distributors, partners, vendors, and other third parties. Review customer ownership structures, corporate affiliations, beneficial ownership information, and geographic presence. Assess customer-provided information for completeness and identify potential red flags. Support enhanced due diligence investigations when elevated risks are identified. Maintain accurate records of KYC reviews and associated compliance determinations. Restricted Party Screening Perform restricted-party screening using Descartes and other approved screening tools. Screen customers, end users, vendors, financial institutions, intermediaries, resellers, distributors, and other transaction participants against applicable sanctions and restricted-party lists. Review and resolve potential screening matches. Coordinate escalation of possible sanctions or export-control concerns. Ensure screening is conducted at required points throughout the transaction lifecycle, including new transactions, customer updates, renewals, and other triggering events. Sales Opportunity Reviews Review sales opportunities and transactions for export control and sanctions compliance concerns. Verify customer locations, end users, end uses, and transaction details. Identify transactions involving elevated-risk countries, entities, government organizations, or industries. Support review of reseller, distributor, and channel partner transactions. Work with Sales Operations and Legal teams to resolve compliance-related questions before transactions proceed. Export Compliance Operations Support routine EAR and ITAR compliance activities. Review requests involving international shipments, software access, demonstrations, evaluations, training, and customer engagements. Assist with export authorization tracking and record maintenance. Monitor compliance queues and ensure timely completion of required reviews. Maintain trade compliance databases, logs, and other operational records. Compliance Documentation and Reporting Maintain organized records supporting compliance reviews and screening decisions. Prepare routine metrics, reports, and dashboards relating to compliance activities. Assist with internal audits and compliance assessments. Support responses to internal and external information requests. Help maintain compliance procedures, work instructions, and training materials. Cross-Functional Collaboration Partner with Sales, Customer Success, Finance, Procurement, Human Resources, IT, and Legal teams. Provide guidance regarding routine compliance procedures and screening requirements. Escalate unusual, complex, or higher-risk transactions to senior compliance personnel. Assist with employee training and awareness initiatives. What We're Looking For Bachelor's degree in Business, International Relations, Political Science, Criminal Justice, Supply Chain, Finance, Law, Public Policy, or a related field. Experience in trade compliance, compliance operations, risk management, due diligence, investigations, legal operations, or a related field. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Exceptional attention to detail and organizational abilities. Ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Proficiency with Microsoft Office, including Excel. Nice To Have Skills Experience conducting customer due diligence, KYC reviews, sanctions screening, or compliance reviews. Familiarity with EAR, ITAR, OFAC sanctions regulations, or other trade compliance frameworks. Experience using Descartes, World-Check, Dow Jones, or similar screening tools. Knowledge of Salesforce, CRM systems, or case-management platforms. Experience working in a legal, compliance, financial crime, risk, or regulatory environment. Position Type : New Position Magnet Is Proud To Offer Benefits Such As Generous time off policies Competitive compensation Volunteer opportunities Reward and recognition programs Employee committees & resource groups Healthcare and retirement benefits Indicators of Success We’re looking for someone who checks off most, but not all, of the boxes listed in “skills and experiences”. It’s more important to us to find candidates who can display indicators of success through skills they have developed and experiences they have been a part of, than to find folks who have “been there, done that”. We want to be part of your development journey, and we’ll learn as much from you as you learn from us. How We Work At Magnet Forensics, we take a hybrid-flexible approach to support your productivity and work-life balance. If you’re within a comfortable travel distance to one of our offices, you’ll occasionally join us in person. How often you’ll come in depends on your department and team needs, typically ranging from weekly to monthly. These in-person moments help us build stronger connections, spark new ideas, and celebrate our successes together. Most days, you can choose what works best for you, while staying in tune with your team’s goals. We’re excited to welcome you to our team and look forward to achieving great things together - both in the office and wherever you work best! The Most Important Thing We’re looking for candidates that can provide examples of how they have demonstrated Magnet CODE in their previous experiences: CARE – We care about each other and our mission to make a difference in the world. OWN – We are accountable for our results – while never forgetting to act with integrity, empathy, and respect. DEDICATE – We put our heart and soul into meeting the needs of our customers and helping them serve the people they protect. EVOLVE – We are constantly innovating and exploring new ways to work together to make an impact with our work. Here at Magnet Forensics, we are committed to continuous learning and are focused on building a diverse and inclusive workforce. This commitment will be reflected in our hiring processes and embedded in our values and how we treat one another. If you’re interested in this role, but do not meet all of the qualifications listed above, we encourage you to apply anyways. Magnet Forensics is an Equal Opportunity Employer and considers applicants for employment without regard to race, colour, religion, sex, orientation, national origin, age, disability, genetics or any other basis forbidden under federal, provincial, or local law. We are committed to providing an inclusive, accessible recruitment process and work environment. Accommodation is available to all applicants upon request throughout the hiring process. Please contact [email protected] should you require any accommodations. All offers of employment at Magnet are contingent upon satisfactory completion of a background check. All background checks will be conducted in accordance with all applicable laws. Magnet will consider each position’s job duties, among other factors, in determining what constitutes satisfactory completion of the background check. Refusal to consent to a background check may be grounds for revoking an offer of employment. US Applicants: Magnet Forensics participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S. Magnet Forensics handles and uses personal data of job applicants in line with its Recruitment Privacy Policy found here . Magnet does not use artificial intelligence (defined as a machine-based system that infers from input to generate outputs such as predictions, content, recommendations, or decisions) for screening, assessing, or selecting applicants. Should this practice change, we will update this disclosure accordingly.
